newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH BOND YIELDS END LOWER, CROWNS SOFTENS.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH BOND YIELDS END LOWER, CROWNS SOFTENS.

text.p: Swedish bond yields ended lower on Tuesday following a general fall in European yields and the crown softened against the dollar and mark.
European yields fell in relief after the Bundesbank's decision not to raise rates at its repo operation.
"But the market is rather nervous not knowing how the Bundesbank or the Federal Reserve will act rate wise," one dealer said.
Even though the Bundesbank left its repo rate at an unchanged 3.0 percent, the market is already speculating about a change-over to variable rate or an increase next week.
Six month T-bill rate was unchanged at 4.31 percent and the 10-year bond yield fell four basis points to 6.53 percent.
The crown softened to 4.2990 to the mark versus 4.2910 crowns late Monday. It traded in a narrow range 4.2970-4.3100.
"We have seen large two way interest in the crown today. The crown hit the wall at 4.3100," said one dealer, adding that he did not see any signs of intervention by the Riksbank.
The Riksbank left its repo rate unchanged at 4.10 percent its weekly tender as expected by the market.
Dealers said the market was now focusing on U.S. data.
